run_metadata.seed_myth: Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan. It is located on the island of Honshu, about one hundred kilometers southwest of the city of Tokyo. Its height is three thousand seven hundred and seventy-six meters. Mount Fuji is a stratovolcano, which means it is built up of many layers of hardened lava, ash, and rock. The mountain has a nearly symmetrical cone shape and is often shown with a cap of white snow at the top. The last large eruption of Mount Fuji happened in seventeen oh seven, during a period called the Hoei eruption. Scientists still classify the volcano as active, but the chance of an eruption in the near future is considered low. Mount Fuji has been important in Japanese culture for many centuries. It is a sacred mountain in the Shinto religion. Many shrines and temples are built around its base. Each summer, large numbers of people climb to the summit to watch the sunrise from the top. Mount Fuji is also one of the most painted and photographed landscapes in the world. In two thousand thirteen, it was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list.
